relevance_note: Describes one family with HA20 and four named TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) carriers with individual clinical detail: 'Autoimmune thyroiditis was diagnosed in all carriers (I-2, II-1, II-4, III-1) at an early age'.
method_note: Read the whole paper, including the converted supplementary files (supp001 is a figure; supp003 contains methods, a primer table and figure legends, with no patient data beyond ages and sex already in the main text). The paper has no patient tables; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON from values I read, and checked spans. Labels are the pedigree labels (I-2, II-1, II-4, III-1), the form the paper uses most; II-1 and III-1 are also called 'patients 1' and '2' in figure legends. Non-carrier or untested relatives are shown only in the pedigree figure, not described in text, so they get no rows. II-4: sex and relationship to the others are not stated. I-2 is called an 'obligate carrier'; no genotyping of her is reported. Ages '30 years' (II-1) and '8 years' (III-1) are the ages given with the PBMC samples in the figure 4/5 legends; recorded as age at last evaluation. age_at_diagnosis: III-1 = age at diagnosis of polyarticular JIA ('at the age of 4 years'); the others = 'at an early age', the stated timing of the autoimmune thyroiditis diagnosis. No age at HA20/genetic diagnosis is given. Inheritance left 'not reported' for all: the paper does not state the parental origin explicitly (only that I-2, mother of the index, is an obligate carrier and III-1 is the index's daughter). Wording differences, not contradictions: the figure 1 legend says 'severe autoinflammatory lung reaction' and adds 'genital papillomatosis', which the Results text omits ('severe inflammatory lung reaction'). Checklist judgements: 'articular symptoms' -> arthritis or arthralgia observed; atrophic gastritis -> GI inflammation observed; psoriasis -> skin lesions observed; repeated genital HSV infections -> recurrent infections observed; anaemia left 'not reported' for cytopenia (autoimmune) because an autoimmune cause is not stated; the lung reaction is not called interstitial lung disease, so that item is 'not reported'; I-2's liver failure is not called autoimmune hepatitis. Patient-cell laboratory findings (raised IL-1β/IL-18 secretion, plasma IL-18) are recorded as functional evidence on the variant rows, not as phenotypic features; the same variant-level functional statement is given for all four carriers. No excluded features: the paper states no feature as absent for any person.

functional_evidence_statement.value: NF-κB luciferase reporter in HEK293 cells: p.(Lys91*) mutant failed to inhibit TNF-α-induced NF-κB activation, suggesting haploinsufficiency; only an N-terminal fragment is produced; severely impaired protein–protein interactome (AP-MS and BioID); elevated IL-1β and IL-18 secretion in carrier PBMCs, suppressed by the caspase-8 inhibitor Z-IETD-FMK
span: The wt A20 dose-dependently inhibited TNF-α induced NF-κB pathway activation, whereas the p.(Lys91*) mutant failed to do so, clearly suggesting a haploinsufficiency (figure 2C)
the p.(Lys91*) mutant was detected only with an N-terminal tag (figure 2A), suggesting that only an N-terminal fragment is produced and no alternative start codons are used
The protein–protein interactome of p.(Lys91*) mutant A20 was severely impaired
We found elevated secretion of IL-1β and IL-18 in PBMCs of the TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) carriers
caspase-8 inhibitor Z-IETD-FMK efficiently suppressed IL-1β and IL-18 secretion in PBMCs of the TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*)-positive patients
